current: qip_edge::cell::Cell::work (backend/crates/edge/qip-edge/src/cell.rs) never calls out to the centre on its hot path, by construction (ADR 0008). A cell trades on a pre-granted, signed, expiring CapitalEnvelope, and it stops only when that envelope's own clock runs out (the envelope_expiry gate), whatever hosts the centre. When the policy payload goes stale, the cell narrows to the 0.375 sizing floor and publishes the capability as stale; it does not stop. This is reached from production through qip-edge-node's serve loop (main.rs), which logs a failed mesh exchange and still runs run_pass -> Cell::work under the simulated feed, the only feed the node accepts. Nothing stops the cell on loss of the centre except a halt the centre itself issued.

current: The in-tree event fabric (ADR 0100) holds part of this as a library, and nothing deploys it. qip_streaming::event_fabric::broker::Broker keeps a file-backed, checkpointed log: a consumer group that committed N resumes at N+1 after a broker restart with no gap and no overlap, and a fresh consumer can replay from any retained offset. On a stream declared RefuseProducer (the P0/P1 class), the same broker refuses a produce once any checkpointed group trails the high watermark by more than the stream's lag_limit (FABRIC-049). So with every consumer stopped it accepts lag_limit more batches and then stops accepting, which for those streams is the opposite of this requirement's check; a stream declared to tolerate a backlog keeps accepting. No production path opens a Broker: qip-fabricd refuses to start, and a search of qip-edge-node/src/main.rs finds no reference to the producer-side event_fabric module. No regional service plane exists to lose (C3).
evidence: infrastructure/event-fabric/streams.local.json (control.local and reflex-outcomes.local are refuse_producer, lag_limit 256 and 4096)
backend/crates/apps/qip-fabricd/src/main.rs (refuses to start; config, health and archiver are stubs)
gap: Three things. No production path opens the broker, so nothing journals in any deployment. There is no regional service plane to stop, so the chaos check cannot be run. And this requirement conflicts with FABRIC-049 on RefuseProducer streams: with every consumer stopped the broker stops accepting after lag_limit batches instead of journaling through the outage. Which rule holds for a group that is down rather than slow needs a decision record; no code should pick one silently.
